description: A studio-style team project in which students take a game from pitch to vertical slice to release candidate, run playtests, read telemetry and write a postmortem. In the lab they work through branching production cases, plan schedules and risks, and analyse test data.
modelledOn: Schell, The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses
Game Accessibility Guidelines (community standard) and the postmortem format used in game industry magazines
outcomes: Write a concept pitch and scope plan with pillars, a cut list and a risk register for a game aimed at a stated audience.
Organise a team with clear roles, a sprint process and a version-controlled production pipeline.
Plan and run iterative prototypes and playtests, and turn observations and telemetry into design changes.
Define and deliver a vertical slice and pass milestone reviews against stated quality criteria.
Prepare a game for release with a quality, localisation and store-readiness checklist.
Write a postmortem, a technical report and a portfolio piece that record the project honestly and show individual contribution.

units.title: Concept pitch and scope control
topics: High concept, design pillars, target audience and a one-page pitch
Players and platforms in Ghana and West Africa: low-end Android, data costs, mobile money and offline play
Scope control: MoSCoW priorities, the cut list and feature freeze
Business models and monetisation: premium, ad-supported, in-app purchase and the ethics of each
Risk register, feasibility study and the game design document as a living document

units.title: Studio team roles and pipelines
topics: Roles: producer, designer, programmer, artist, audio, QA and community; how responsibilities overlap in a small team
Agile for games: sprints, backlogs, kanban boards, stand-ups and retrospectives
Production pipeline: version control for code and art, build automation and naming conventions
Team charter, communication with unreliable connectivity and resolving conflict
Estimating tasks and planning milestones with Gantt charts and critical path

units.title: Iterative prototyping
topics: Paper prototypes and greyboxing to test mechanics before art
Core loop analysis and the MDA framework of mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics
Throwaway prototypes versus evolutionary prototypes; deciding what to keep
Game feel and feedback: timing, animation, sound and screen response
Technical risk spikes: testing the hardest feature first

units.title: Playtesting and telemetry review
topics: Planning a playtest: goals, recruiting players, protocol and consent
Observation and questionnaires: think-aloud, interviews, usability scales and engagement surveys
Telemetry design: event schema, funnels, retention at day 1 and day 7, and privacy limits
Reading data to balance difficulty and economy, and detecting where players quit
Accessibility and inclusive design testing: colour, controls, text size and cognitive load

units.title: Vertical slice and milestone reviews
topics: Milestone ladder: concept, first playable, vertical slice, alpha, beta, release candidate
Defining the vertical slice and setting its quality bar
Running a milestone review: demo, metrics, risks and decisions to continue, cut or cancel
Sustainable pace: avoiding crunch, burn-down charts and cutting scope early
Integration, build stability and keeping the game always playable

units.title: Quality, localisation and platform readiness
topics: QA process: test plans, bug reporting, severity and priority, and triage meetings
Compatibility and performance on target devices, including low-memory phones
Localisation and internationalisation: English, French, Twi, Hausa and right-to-left text
Legal matters: licences for engines and assets, music rights, age ratings and children's data
Store listing, compliance checks and payment integration

units.title: Release preparation and postmortem
topics: Launch plan: store page, trailer, press kit, community channels and soft launch
Live operations: patching, event calendars and handling player support
Success metrics: downloads, retention, revenue per user and review scores
The postmortem format: what went right, what went wrong and what to change
Handling a failed launch, a critical bug or a negative public reaction

units.title: Technical report and portfolio
topics: Structure of a technical report: problem, design decisions, implementation, evaluation, limitations
Portfolio pieces: playable build, gameplay video, design breakdowns and a case study
Individual contribution statements and fair peer assessment
Final showcase: presenting to a panel and answering critical questions
Career pathways in African and global game studios, freelancing and funding

schedule.title: Pitching a game
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page pitch for a game set in a Ghanaian market, with three pillars, the target player, platform limits and a first cut list.

tasks.title: Rank five game pitches against the given rubric for clarity of pillars and audience and justify the highest and lowest scores
Choose the platform and feature set for a game aimed at players on 2 GB phones with expensive data, citing the evidence in the case
Cut a 40-feature backlog to fit a 10-week team schedule using MoSCoW, defending each cut against producer and designer objections

schedule.title: Business models and risk
schedule.exercise: Compare premium, ad-supported and in-app purchase models for your pitch, and list ten risks with probability, impact and an owner.

tasks.title: Build a risk register as a table of ten risks with probability, impact, score and mitigation, sorted by score
Choose a monetisation model for a children's puzzle game and handle a case where the publisher requests loot boxes
Model revenue for ad-supported and paid versions using download, retention and conversion estimates over 12 months and plot break-even

schedule.title: Teams, process and pipelines
schedule.exercise: Write a team charter with roles and decision rules, set up a sprint board with the first 20 tasks, and draw the critical path to the first-playable milestone.

tasks.title: Assign a six-person team to the listed project tasks, making sure no role is overloaded or left without an owner
Draw a Gantt chart for a 13-week project with dependencies and mark the critical path to the first-playable milestone
Set up a repository with branches, a build script and a rule file for large art assets, then merge two conflicting changes from two artists

schedule.title: Paper prototypes and core loops
schedule.exercise: Paper-prototype your core loop, run it with two players, and write down which mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics each tester reported.

tasks.title: Evaluate three paper prototype test reports and decide for each whether to continue, change or drop the mechanic with reasons
Draw the core loop of a given mobile game with rewards and decision points and label the mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics
Decide which of four prototypes to evolve, which to throw away and what to carry forward, justified by the test evidence and the schedule

schedule.title: Game feel and technical spikes
schedule.exercise: List ten feedback effects for jumping and landing in your game, and design a one-day spike to test the riskiest technical feature.

tasks.title: Rate six versions of a jump described by timing and feedback settings for game feel and explain what makes the best one work
Plan a two-day technical spike on multiplayer over weak networks, with the question, success test and fallback if it fails
Run the spike case: interpret benchmark results on three phones, decide whether the feature is feasible and renegotiate scope with the producer

schedule.title: Planning and running playtests
schedule.exercise: Write a playtest plan for ten players with goals, tasks, consent text and a questionnaire, and define six telemetry events with their fields.

tasks.title: Pick suitable participants and a protocol from a case file for a playtest of a farming game and justify the choices
Compute the mean and spread of a usability scale from 12 questionnaire responses and identify the weakest-rated aspect
Design an event table for a mobile game and write SQL for day 1 and day 7 retention from a supplied log of 5,000 sessions

schedule.title: From data to design changes
schedule.exercise: Use funnel data to find the level where most players quit, propose two design changes, and check the build against five accessibility guidelines.

tasks.title: Audit a game screen description against five accessibility guidelines and list the failures with a fix for each
Query a level completion table to find where players quit and how long successful players spend on each level
Tune an enemy health value using simulated win rates from 1,000 runs so the target win rate is 60 percent for novices

schedule.title: Milestones and the vertical slice
schedule.exercise: Define the vertical slice for your game, write its quality bar as ten checkable statements, and prepare the agenda for a milestone review.

tasks.title: Draw a milestone ladder for the project with entry and exit criteria at each rung and the weeks they are due
Judge whether a described build meets the vertical slice quality bar and list the gaps that must close before the review
Present a milestone review to a mock publisher, answering five hard questions on risk and budget, and score the decision to continue or cut

schedule.title: Sustainable pace and stable builds
schedule.exercise: Draw a burn-down chart from sprint data, show where scope must be cut, and set the rules that keep the main branch always playable.

tasks.title: Plot a burn-down chart from sprint data and mark when the team would finish at the current pace
Handle a case where the team faces a deadline with 30 percent of work left, choosing cuts instead of crunch and explaining it to the team
Set up a build check that runs tests on every merge and blocks a deliberately broken commit from reaching the main branch

schedule.title: Quality assurance, localisation and store readiness
schedule.exercise: Write a test plan and a release checklist covering device compatibility, two translations, music licences, age rating and the store listing.

tasks.title: Triage 20 bug reports by severity and priority and decide which five must be fixed before release
Extract all strings from a small game into a table, translate to two languages and test that long text does not overflow the interface
Resolve a licensing dispute over a music track and a children's data question before store submission, and score the release decision

schedule.title: Launching and operating a game
schedule.exercise: Prepare a launch plan with a soft-launch region, a community channel, a support process and the five metrics you will watch in the first month.

tasks.title: Assemble a launch checklist for a mobile game in Ghana and mark which items are done, late or missing from the case file
Compute downloads, retention and revenue per user for the first 30 days from supplied data and compare with the targets
Run a live-operations case: plan a patch, an event and a compensation for a server outage within the budget and player trust limits

schedule.title: Postmortems and crisis handling
schedule.exercise: Write the postmortem for your own project in the what went right, what went wrong and what we will change format, with evidence for each point.

tasks.title: Sort the statements of a sample postmortem into went right, went wrong or change next time, and note any lacking evidence
Draw a cause-and-effect diagram of why a game launched late and mark the root cause and two contributing factors
Respond to a launch day crash and a viral negative review thread, choosing actions in order and scored on honesty, speed and recovery

schedule.title: Report, portfolio and showcase
schedule.exercise: Produce a technical report outline, a portfolio page for your build, a fair contribution statement for each team member and a five-minute showcase script.

tasks.title: Lay out the sections of a technical report as an outline diagram and note the evidence each section needs from the project
Assess fairness in a team case with uneven work and write contribution statements and a peer assessment that match the evidence
Defend your project to a mock panel on design choices, results and limits, and respond to five critical questions scored on the rubric
